scope: Formulaic provenance-first wording in both strengthened arguments and the opening sentence of all six reinforcing arguments.

changedFields.title: Christian plausibility defense thesis
changedFields.beforeOpening: As an AI-generated synthesis, a qualified Christianity could remain plausible if cumulative evidence warrants commitment without certainty, sincere truth-seeking can permit salvation without explicit assent, and annihilation replaces eternal torment.
changedFields.afterOpening: A carefully qualified form of Christianity could remain plausible if cumulative evidence warrants commitment without certainty, sincere truth-seeking can permit salvation without explicit assent, and annihilation replaces eternal conscious torment.

changedFields.title: Christian plausibility defense conclusion
changedFields.beforeOpening: On this hypothetical AI reconstruction, Christianity could therefore remain plausible: arguments need only shift confidence, sincere seekers may receive salvation without correct theological propositions, and annihilation may replace endless punishment.
changedFields.afterOpening: Qualified Christianity could therefore remain plausible on this reconstruction: arguments need only shift confidence, sincere seekers may still receive salvation without correct theological propositions, and annihilation may replace endless punishment.

changedFields.title: Calibrated accessibility
changedFields.beforeOpening: An AI-generated extension could treat divine hiddenness as justified only within a calibrated accessibility constraint.
changedFields.afterOpening: A calibrated-accessibility model would justify divine hiddenness only under strict conditions that protect meaningful choice.

changedFields.title: Justice-based inclusivism
changedFields.beforeOpening: An AI-developed extension could hold that justice should track a person's responsible orientation toward truth, not theological vocabulary that assent may make unavailable.
changedFields.afterOpening: A justice-based inclusivist model would ultimately judge people by their responsible orientation toward truth, not by their ability to affirm particular theological language.

changedFields.title: Finite consequences
changedFields.beforeOpening: An AI-developed extension could make annihilation permissible only after a person persistently refuses a relationship whose availability and stakes have become adequately clear.
changedFields.afterOpening: On a finite-consequences account, annihilation would be permissible only after a person refused a relationship whose availability and stakes had become adequately clear.

changedFields.title: Hiddenness and hell challenge thesis
changedFields.beforeOpening: As an AI-generated synthesis, the con case holds that a perfectly loving relational God would make divine availability evident to every capable person, because awareness enables free acceptance without coercing love.
changedFields.afterOpening: The strongest version of the hiddenness challenge holds that a perfectly loving relational God would make divine availability evident to every capable person, because awareness enables free acceptance without coercing love.

changedFields.title: Hiddenness and hell challenge conclusion
changedFields.beforeOpening: This AI-generated conclusion infers that, if even one sincere nonbeliever lacks awareness of an available loving God, freedom does not explain that hiddenness, which therefore weighs against such a God's existence.
changedFields.afterOpening: If even one sincere nonbeliever lacks awareness of an available loving God, then freedom alone does not adequately explain that hiddenness, which therefore weighs as evidence against such a God's existence.

changedFields.title: Recognition without coercion
changedFields.beforeOpening: A possible extension is that divine disclosure could secure ordinary, settled awareness of God's availability without determining anyone's response.
changedFields.afterOpening: In a well-calibrated recognition-without-coercion model, divine disclosure could secure ordinary, settled awareness of God's availability without determining anyone's response.

changedFields.title: Epistemic equality
changedFields.beforeOpening: One possible extension is that a just relational salvation system would need to neutralize arbitrary differences in culture, temperament, available evidence, and cognitive style.
changedFields.afterOpening: Under a demanding epistemic-equality constraint, a just relational salvation system would need to neutralize arbitrary differences in culture, temperament, available evidence, and cognitive style.

changedFields.title: Less costly worlds
changedFields.beforeOpening: One possible extension is to compare hiddenness with a world in which God's existence is ordinarily well supported without being absolutely certain.
changedFields.afterOpening: A comparison asks us to consider a less costly world in which God's existence is ordinarily well supported without being absolutely certain.
